,"recipeIngredient": [
"2 1/2 pounds chicken thighs and drumsticks",
"8 teaspoons sweet paprika, divided",
"3 tablespoons olive oil, divided",
"Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper",
"2 medium onions, finely chopped (about 2 cups)",
"2 red bell peppers, seeded and sliced into 1/2-inch strips",
"3/4 cup homemade or store-bought low-sodium chicken stock, divided",
"1 tablespoon all-purpose flour",
"1 (14-ounce) can whole tomatoes, chopped with juice reserved (see note)",
"2 tablespoons sour cream",
"1 tablespoon chopped parsley" ]
,"recipeInstructions": [
{
"@type": "HowToStep"
,"text": "Pat chicken dry and place in bowl with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Stir 5 teaspoons paprika plus 1 teaspoon salt in small bowl. Add paprika mixture to chicken and coat well. Cover and chill at least 4 hours, and preferably overnight (see note)."
} ,{
"@type": "HowToStep"
,"text": "Heat 1 tablespoon oil in large Dutch oven over medium high heat until shimmering. Add half of chicken to Dutch oven and cook chicken until well browned, 4 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to plate, add remaining tablespoon oil, and repeat with second batch of chicken. Set chicken aside."
} ,{
"@type": "HowToStep"
,"text": "Reduce heat to medium and add onions and 1 teaspoon salt. Cook until onions are softened, stirring frequently, 6 to 8 minutes. Add peppers, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, and remaining tablespoon paprika and cook, stirring, for 1 minute."
} ,{
"@type": "HowToStep"
,"text": "Stir 2 tablespoons chicken broth into flour and add to pot. Cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Whisk in remaining chicken broth and tomatoes (with juice), and bring to simmer. Nestle in chicken, skin side up, cover, and reduce heat to low. Gently simmer until chicken is completely tender, about 30 minutes."
} ,{
"@type": "HowToStep"
,"text": "Transfer chicken to plate, stir in sour cream, season to taste, and return chicken to pot. Sprinkle with parsley and serve (see note)."
} ]
,"recipeYield": "4"

"author": {
"@type": "Person",
"name": "marksinmansupergenius"
},
"reviewBody": "There's a step missing - I'll call it 5.1.\n\n\"Transfer chicken to plate, then using immersion blender, puree the sauce. Whisk in sour cream. \" Lolz\n\nSeriously though, this recipe is solid. The best part is the browning of the paprika-rubbed chicken - I thought my girlfriend was going to steal all of the chicken and leave me with only the sauce!"
}
,
{
"@type": "Review",
"author": {
"@type": "Person",
"name": "Jenny C."
},
"reviewBody": "Is there a trick to browning the chicken without burning the rub? I made this last night and it turned out beautifully, but I had to wash my pot between browning and braising because there was so much burnt paprika stuck to the bottom, and it didn't smell like it was going to taste good."
}
,
{
"@type": "Review",
"author": {
"@type": "Person",
"name": "OneWallKitchen"
},
"reviewBody": "Oh, you're killin' me--this is one of my favorite dishes. My friend, whose family is Hungarian, introduced it to me and tries to make it for me once a year even though she's taught me how to make it. The key is she's the one with the nokedli maker--traditional Hungarian dumplings. Another friend made his version for me and served it over egg noodles--still delicious, but just not the same. I've had it over rice and mashed potatoes, but those tiny dumplings are just perfect for chicken paprikash!"
}
,
{
"@type": "Review",
"author": {
"@type": "Person",
"name": "woohoo"
},
"reviewBody": "My Hungarian mother would have chuckled at this recipe's calling for a chintzy 2T of sour cream… Her chicken Paprikash had at least a 1/2 C, and her chicken broth covered the chicken in the pot -- forget that 3/4C that this recipe calls for! Otherwise the ingredients are pretty right on, although the addition of tomato wasn't on her recipe list. I'll have to try it sometime.\n\nAs I grew older and more into foodie-dom, I started to use smoked Spanish Sweet or Bittersweet Paprika for fantabulous taste. I'm going to have to try marinating it overnight to increase flavor, although the smoked paprika will definitely boost flavor even if you don't overnight it.\n\nMy mother always made it with elbow macaroni, which beautifully soaked up the marvelous sauce. Also, doesn't matter what color the bell peppers are (Mom always used green) - just doesn't make a difference. And a final also… use a cut up whole chicken, legs, wings, thighs, whatever you got. Doesn't really matter. Enjoy!"
}
,
{
"@type": "Review",
"author": {
"@type": "Person",
"name": "christocc"
},
"reviewBody": "Also, rather than using kitchen shears in the can of tomatoes (which can damage the shears), the easiest way to break the tomatoes up is with your hand. Strain the tomatoes (to reserve the juice, strain the can into a bowl). Place the tomatoes in a bowl and squish them with your fingers...easiest way I know of!"
}

<div class="loc section-content section__content "><div id="structured-project__steps_1-0" class="comp structured-project__steps mntl-sc-page mntl-block text-passage structured-content" data-sc-sticky-offset="60" data-sc-ad-label-height="24" data-sc-ad-track-spacing="100" data-sc-min-track-height="250" data-sc-max-track-height="600" data-sc-breakpoint="50em" data-sc-load-immediate="1" data-sc-content-positions="[300,600,900,1200,1500,1800,2100]" data-bind-scroll-on-start="true"><OL id="mntl-sc-block_3-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-startgroup mntl-sc-block-group--OL">
<LI id="mntl-sc-block_4-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-startgroup mntl-sc-block-group--LI">
<p id="mntl-sc-block_5-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Pat chicken dry and place in bowl with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Stir 5 teaspoons paprika plus 1 teaspoon salt in small bowl. Add paprika mixture to chicken and coat well. Cover and chill at least 4 hours, and preferably overnight (see note).
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_6-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
</LI>
<LI id="mntl-sc-block_8-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-startgroup mntl-sc-block-group--LI">
<p id="mntl-sc-block_9-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Heat 1 tablespoon oil in large Dutch oven over medium high heat until shimmering. Add half of chicken to Dutch oven and cook chicken until well browned, 4 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to plate, add remaining tablespoon oil, and repeat with second batch of chicken. Set chicken aside.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_10-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
</LI>
<LI id="mntl-sc-block_12-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-startgroup mntl-sc-block-group--LI">
<p id="mntl-sc-block_13-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Reduce heat to medium and add onions and 1 teaspoon salt. Cook until onions are softened, stirring frequently, 6 to 8 minutes. Add peppers, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, and remaining tablespoon paprika and cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_14-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
</LI>
<LI id="mntl-sc-block_16-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-startgroup mntl-sc-block-group--LI">
<p id="mntl-sc-block_17-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Stir 2 tablespoons chicken broth into flour and add to pot. Cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Whisk in remaining chicken broth and tomatoes (with juice), and bring to simmer. Nestle in chicken, skin side up, cover, and reduce heat to low. Gently simmer until chicken is completely tender, about 30 minutes.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_18-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
</LI>
<LI id="mntl-sc-block_20-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-startgroup mntl-sc-block-group--LI">
<p id="mntl-sc-block_21-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Transfer chicken to plate, stir in sour cream, season to taste, and return chicken to pot. Sprinkle with parsley and serve (see note).
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_22-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
</LI>
</OL>
